cards.canonical_statement: Six equal boxes containing eight pencils each contain forty-eight pencils in total.
cards.proof_strategy: Represent equal groups by multiplication and evaluate the product.
sketch_steps: model: Treat the six boxes as six equal groups of eight.

cards.canonical_statement: For all real a and b, four groups of a plus four groups of b equal four groups of a+b.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="a"/><OMV name="b"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>4</OMI><OMV name="a"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>4</OMI><OMV name="b"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>4</OMI><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="a"/><OMV name="b"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Use the distributive law to justify combining two same-sized collections of groups.
sketch_steps: setup: Regard a and b as the amounts in two parts of each group.

cards.canonical_statement: If four equally priced notebooks cost 600 yen in total, then one notebook costs 150 yen.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="p"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>4</OMI><OMV name="p"/></OMA><OMI>600</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="p"/><OMI>150</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Translate total cost as item count times unit price, then divide by four.
sketch_steps: model: Let p be the price of one notebook and write 4p=600.

cards.canonical_statement: Three fourths divided by two fifths equals fifteen eighths.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMI>4</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMI>2</OMI><OMI>5</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMI>15</OMI><OMI>8</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Multiply by the reciprocal and reduce the resulting fraction.
sketch_steps: rewrite: Replace division by 2/5 with multiplication by 5/2.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real x, three fifths of x equals three times x divided by five.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMI>5</OMI></OMA><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMI>5</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Regroup multiplication and division to justify the equivalent symbolic forms.
sketch_steps: reassociate: Move x into the numerator product.

cards.canonical_statement: If three fourths of a real number x is 18, then x is 24.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMI>4</OMI></OMA><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMI>18</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>24</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Represent the stated fraction of the unknown, then multiply by the reciprocal.
sketch_steps: model: Translate three fourths of x as (3/4)x.
solve: Multiply both sides of (3/4)x=18 by 4/3.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real x, if 3x+5=20, then x=5.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMI>5</OMI></OMA><OMI>20</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>5</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Subtract five and divide by the nonzero coefficient three.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real x, 2x-6=10 if and only if x=8.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>2</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMI>6</OMI></OMA><OMI>10</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>8</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Use reversible addition and division steps in both directions.
sketch_steps: forward: Add 6 and divide by 2 to obtain x=8.
conclude: The equation and solution are equivalent.

cards.canonical_statement: The fare with base charge 120 yen and rate 80 yen per kilometre totals 440 yen only when distance d is 4 kilometres.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="d"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMI>120</OMI><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>80</OMI><OMV name="d"/></OMA></OMA><OMI>440</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="d"/><OMI>4</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Translate base charge plus rate times distance into a linear equation and solve it.
sketch_steps: interpret: The distance d is 4 kilometres.

cards.canonical_statement: For all real x and y, if x+y=7 and x-y=1, then x=4 and y=3.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMI>7</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMI>1</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>4</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="y"/><OMI>3</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Add the equations to eliminate y, then substitute the resulting x-value.
sketch_steps: eliminate: Add the two equations to obtain 2x=8.

cards.canonical_statement: For all real x, y, a, and b, if x+y=a and x-y=b, then 2x=a+b.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/><OMV name="a"/><OMV name="b"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMV name="a"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMV name="b"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>2</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="a"/><OMV name="b"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Add the two equalities and justify cancellation of the opposite y-terms.
sketch_steps: add: Add corresponding sides of both equations.

cards.canonical_statement: If 10 tickets consist of 500-yen adult tickets and 300-yen child tickets and cost 3800 yen, then there are 4 adult and 6 child tickets.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="a"/><OMV name="b"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="a"/><OMV name="b"/></OMA><OMI>10</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>500</OMI><OMV name="a"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>300</OMI><OMV name="b"/></OMA></OMA><OMI>3800</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="a"/><OMI>4</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="b"/><OMI>6</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Model ticket count and total cost as a simultaneous linear system and eliminate one variable.
sketch_steps: eliminate: Subtract 300 times the count equation from the cost equation.
interpret: a=4 adult tickets and b=6 child tickets.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real x, if x^2-5x+6=0, then x=2 or x=3.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>5</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA></OMA><OMI>6</OMI></OMA><OMI>0</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="or"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>3</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Factor the quadratic as (x-2)(x-3) and apply the zero-product property.
sketch_steps: split: A zero product has at least one zero factor.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real x, x^2=9 if and only if x=3 or x=-3.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMI>9</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="or"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>3</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="unary_minus"/><OMI>3</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Use the difference-of-squares factorization and verify both roots for the reverse direction.

cards.canonical_statement: If positive rectangle width x and length x+2 have area 48, then the width is 6.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="lt"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMV name="x"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMI>48</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>6</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Translate the area condition into a quadratic, solve both algebraic roots, and keep the positive length.
sketch_steps: filter: Reject x=-8 because a width is positive; conclude x=6.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real x, 3x-7≤5 if and only if x≤4.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>3</OMI><OMV name="x"/></OMA><OMI>7</OMI></OMA><OMI>5</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>4</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Add seven and divide by the positive coefficient three, preserving the inequality direction.
sketch_steps: divide: Divide by positive 3 without reversing the inequality.

cards.canonical_statement: For all real x and y, x≤y if and only if -y≤-x.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="unary_minus"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="unary_minus"/><OMV name="x"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Multiply both sides by -1 and justify reversal of the order relation in both directions.
sketch_steps: forward: Multiply x≤y by -1 and reverse the inequality.
reverse: Apply the same operation to -y≤-x.
conclude: The two inequalities are equivalent.

cards.canonical_statement: If real ride count n is nonnegative and the 1200-yen pass plus 350 yen per ride costs at most 4000 yen, then n≤8.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="n"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMV name="n"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMI>1200</OMI><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>350</OMI><OMV name="n"/></OMA></OMA><OMI>4000</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMV name="n"/><OMI>8</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Translate the budget cap into a linear inequality, isolate the ride count, and interpret the bound.
sketch_steps: solve: Subtract 1200 and divide by positive 350 to obtain n≤8.
interpret: The budget permits at most eight rides.

hard_negatives.query: Six equal boxes containing eight pencils each contain fourteen pencils in total.
hard_negatives.reason: Confuses multiplication of equal groups with addition of the two visible numbers.

hard_negatives.query: For all real a and b, 4a+4b=8(a+b).
hard_negatives.reason: Incorrectly adds the common coefficient while factoring it.

hard_negatives.query: If four equally priced notebooks cost 600 yen, one notebook costs 2400 yen.
hard_negatives.reason: Multiplies the total by the item count instead of dividing it.

hard_negatives.query: Three fourths divided by two fifths equals six twentieths.
hard_negatives.reason: Multiplies the fractions without taking the reciprocal of the divisor.
Replaces multiplication in the numerator with addition.

hard_negatives.query: If three fourths of x is 18, then x is 27/2.
hard_negatives.reason: Multiplies 18 by 3/4 instead of by the reciprocal 4/3.

hard_negatives.query: For every real x, if 3x+5=20, then x=25/3.
hard_negatives.reason: Adds five instead of subtracting five before division.

hard_negatives.query: For every real x, 2x-6=10 if and only if x=2.
hard_negatives.reason: Moves the constant with the wrong sign before dividing.

hard_negatives.query: A fare with base charge 120 yen and rate 80 yen per kilometre is modeled by 120d+80=440.
hard_negatives.reason: Swaps the fixed base charge and the per-kilometre coefficient.

hard_negatives.query: The system x+y=7 and x-y=1 has solution x=3, y=4.
hard_negatives.reason: The proposed pair satisfies the sum but violates the difference equation.
Uses subtraction on the right after adding the two equations.

hard_negatives.query: Ten 500-yen adult and 300-yen child tickets costing 3800 yen consist of 6 adults and 4 children.
hard_negatives.reason: Swaps the counts; the resulting total is 4200 yen.

hard_negatives.query: If x^2-5x+6=0, then x=-2 or x=-3.
hard_negatives.reason: Reads the signs of the roots directly from the factors.

hard_negatives.query: For every real x, x^2=9 if and only if x=3.
hard_negatives.reason: Drops the negative square root and therefore fails the characterization.

hard_negatives.query: A positive rectangle width x with x(x+2)=48 may have width -8.
hard_negatives.reason: Keeps an algebraic root that violates the positive-width premise.

hard_negatives.query: For every real x, 3x-7≤5 if and only if x≤-2/3.
hard_negatives.reason: Moves -7 in the wrong direction before dividing.

hard_negatives.query: For all real x and y, x≤y if and only if -x≤-y.
hard_negatives.reason: Negates both sides without reversing the order relation.

hard_negatives.query: Under 1200+350n≤4000 with n≥0, the budget permits strictly fewer than eight rides.
hard_negatives.reason: Changes the inclusive bound and incorrectly excludes the feasible endpoint n=8.
